tracks.name: Terminal Titans
tracks.description: Build a useful command line tool: file organizer, terminal tutor, backup utility, or Zypper helper.
starterIdeas: Zypper Package Helper with interactive visual search & history rollback
Terminal Tutor: Gamified CLI interactive learning environment in curses/ratatui
Smart File Organizer with automated MIME detection and deduplication
Snapshot aware backup utility integrating with Btrfs/Snapper
tracks.rubricFocus: CLI ergonomics, command line flags (POSIX/GNU standards), documentation, practical daily usefulness.

tracks.name: Root Access
tracks.description: Create a defensive permissions auditor, suspicious login explainer, or hardening assistant. Intermediate to advanced; use only authorized sandbox systems.
starterIdeas: AppArmor Profile Visualizer & interactive policy generator for desktop apps
Defensive sudo / auth.log analyzer explaining anomalous logins in plain English
Systemd Service Hardening Assistant checking ProtectSystem & CapabilityBoundingSet
Container vulnerability scanner tailored for lightweight openSUSE MicroOS images
tracks.rubricFocus: Defensive rigor, sandboxing safety, accuracy of audit rules, privacy first design without credential leakage.

tracks.name: GeekoOps
tracks.description: Improve builds, tests, packaging or deployment: OBS (Open Build Service) status dashboard, openQA explorer or container helper.
starterIdeas: OBS Build Matrix Dashboard with real time SSE build notifications & dependency graph
openQA Visual Test Inspector surfacing needle matching test video diffs
Automated RPM specfile linter & multi architecture test harness
Podman / MicroOS declarative container orchestrator with transactional update verification
tracks.rubricFocus: Integration depth with openSUSE tools (OBS/openQA), reliability, build reproducibility, CI/CD pipeline efficiency.

tracks.name: Desktop Reboot
tracks.description: Improve onboarding, accessibility or everyday desktop use. Examples: accessible launcher, package discovery or setup assistant.
starterIdeas: First Time openSUSE Setup Wizard welcoming users with hardware driver check and curated app bundles
High contrast screen reader optimized launcher for Wayland desktops
Unified Flatpak / RPM package discovery UI with permissions breakdown
Quick YaST Control Center widget for modern desktop system management
tracks.rubricFocus: Design craftsmanship, intuitive onboarding, accessibility (screen reader / keyboard nav), seamless desktop integration.

tracks.name: Upstream Heroes
tracks.description: Address an existing issue with code, documentation, tests, translations or accessibility. All levels. A submitted contribution can qualify without a maintainer merge.
starterIdeas: Resolve confirmed open issues on openSUSE tools (YaST, Zypper, OWS, transactional update)
Write missing documentation, man pages, or interactive guides for Leap / Tumbleweed
Create Hindi, Kannada, Tamil, or Telugu translations for openSUSE desktop tools
Implement automated regression test suites for upstream community utilities
tracks.rubricFocus: Upstream alignment, submission quality, etiquette, clear problem diagnosis, thorough tests/documentation.

tracks.name: What Does Linux Need Next?
tracks.description: Identify a real Linux/openSUSE community need and build an original response. Explain the users, evidence of need and measurable value.
starterIdeas: Offline first Linux documentation and package mirror hub for resource constrained schools
Local LLM CLI copilot trained strictly on openSUSE man pages and wiki guides
Zero config Linux audio & screen casting studio setup tool for educators
Decentralized peer to peer package caching daemon for local campus hackathons
tracks.rubricFocus: Clarity of user need, evidence of research, originality of response, demonstration of measurable community value.

rookieChallenge.title: Repair the Deploy Automation Script
rookieChallenge.description: This shell script meant for backing up configuration files and restarting the openSUSE web service contains 3 deliberate syntax and logic errors. Identify and fix them so it passes the automated test suite.
rookieChallenge.initialCode:
#!/bin/bash
# Backup & Service Check Script - openSUSE BLR 2027
# TASK: Fix the 3 deliberate bugs in this script

BACKUP_DIR="/var/backup/geeko"
TIMESTAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)

# BUG 1: Syntax error in test condition
if [ -d "$BACKUP_DIR"
    echo "Directory exists"
else
    mkdir -p "$BACKUP_DIR"
fi

# BUG 2: Unquoted variable expansion with spaces in path
TARGET_FILE="/etc/geeko config/settings.conf"
tar -czf "$BACKUP_DIR/backup_$TIMESTAMP.tar.gz" $TARGET_FILE

# BUG 3: Inverted exit status check for zypper service
systemctl is-active --quiet apache2
if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "SUCCESS: Service is running smoothly."
    exit 0
else
    echo "ERROR: Service is stopped!"
    exit 1
fi
rookieChallenge.solutionHint: Check missing bracket on line 8, add quotes around $TARGET_FILE on line 16, and check exit status logic on line 20 (0 means active in systemctl).

expertChallenge.title: Diagnose Service Permission & SELinux Sandbox Failure
expertChallenge.description: An isolated openQA worker daemon fails to write artifacts to /srv/obs-worker/data due to restrictive systemd ProtectSystem directives and file ACL permissions. Diagnose the misconfiguration and write the correct override commands.
expertChallenge.errorLog:
systemd[1]: obs-worker.service: Failed at step NAMESPACE spawning /usr/bin/obs-worker: Read-only file system
audit[1842]: AVC apparmor="DENIED" operation="open" profile="/usr/bin/obs-worker" name="/srv/obs-worker/data/build.lock"
obs-worker[1843]: Fatal error: Unable to obtain write lock on /srv/obs-worker/data. Exit code 13 (EACCES)

faq.q: What is openSUSE India – Bengaluru Connect 2027?
faq.a: It is a flagship two-day open source technology conference and 20 hour Buildathon happening in January 2027 at Newton School of Technology, Bengaluru. It unites beginners, college students, Linux enthusiasts, and upstream contributors to learn Linux, master openSUSE tools, and build impactful software.

The Geeko Buildathon is a 20 hour mentored hackathon running from Day 1 at 14:30 IST to Day 2 at 10:30 IST. Up to 83 teams (3–4 builders each, 250 participants total) choose one of six tracks to solve real developer, security, desktop, or community challenges.

faq.q: Do I have to know Linux or openSUSE beforehand?
faq.a: No! The event is specifically designed for all experience levels. Day 1 includes beginner talks and hands on workshops like the 'Linux & openSUSE Starter Lab'. Mentors circulate throughout the 20 hours to guide newcomers.

faq.q: Who is eligible and is there a registration fee?
faq.a: Admission is 100% free! Anyone enthusiastic about open source software (students, working developers, hobbyists) may apply. Strict cap is 250 participants. Teams must have 3 to 4 members. For overnight building, participants must be 18+.

Yes. The planning envelope and venue capacity accommodate all 250 participants overnight. A dedicated quiet rest area, load tested electrical circuits, campus security, and staffed first aid coverage are maintained throughout the night.

The event budget provides: Day 1 welcome refreshments, Day 1 lunch, evening snacks & tea, overnight dinner, late-night snacks, and Day 2 breakfast (280 servings each). IMPORTANT: Day 2 lunch is NOT included. Attendees are informed in advance to arrange lunch from nearby college eateries or food courts.

faq.q: Do all attendees get a free T-shirt?
faq.a: No. In strict accordance with the event's financial plan, only 25 reward T-shirts are budgeted for competition winners (Top 3 teams: up to 12 shirts; Bug Hunt winners: 2; Arcade winners: 4; Quest winners: 2; plus 5 size buffer). Attendees who wish to own an official event T-shirt can purchase or pre-order one via the event merchandise shop.

All submitting teams showcase their projects in the 83-team Demo Arena across 6 parallel lanes. Judges score according to a published 5-point rubric: Real-world problem & usefulness (25%), Technical execution (25%), Linux/openSUSE relevance (20%), Creativity & innovation (15%), and Documentation/demo (15%). Six overall finalists present on the auditorium stage.
